To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mammary tumour-inducing effects of 17beta-estradiol and an oral contraceptive, Enovid, in C3H female mice are counteracted by the chronic administration of the dopamine agonist, 2-bromo-ergocryptin, an efficacious inhibitor pituitary prolacitin secretion.

the mammary gland tumorigenic effects of chronic 17beta-oestradial administration and the oral contraceptive Enavid can be significantly reduced in C3H female mice by concurrent treatment with the prolactin inhibiting drug 2-bromo-a-ergocryptite (CB-154).
the mammary tumourigenic activity of 17 beta-oestradiol in C3H female mice is significantly reduced by the concurrent administration of 2-bromo-alfa-ergocryptin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of oestrogens on mammary gland development and tumorigenesis.
the role of prolactin in mammary carcinogenesis.
the effects of chronic treatment with 2-brom-alpha-ergocripine (CB- 154) on the mammary tumourigenic activity of oestrogen and progestin in C3H female mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oestrogen-induced mammary tumorigensis in C3H mouse mammary gland is mediated by an increased secretion of prolactin.
mammary tumorigensis is not mediated by prolactin in this model system, but that the tumorigenic effects of oestrogen and the anti-oestrogen tamoxifen can be blocked by CB-154.
CB-154 treatment of steroid-treated C3H mice reduces mammary tumour development, and that this reduction is due to a reduction in the mammary hyperplasias which are induced by the steroids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oestrogens, and possibly other steroid hormones, are tumour promoting agents in the mammary glands of C3H mice.
the mammary gland is a target tissue for the action of prolactin and oestrogens, and that the action of these hormones is additive.

oestrogenic compounds, in the presence of a functional corpus luteum, stimulate the development of hyperplastic mammary nodules, which in turn, are precursors of adenocarcinomas in C3H and other strains of mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prolactin plays a significant role in mammary carcinogenesis in C3H mouse models.
we need to be careful about the use of oestrogens, especially for long term use, and to be careful to use the lowest dose possible.

prolactin plays an important role in the development of mammary gland hyperplasias and tumorigenesis, and that the use of CB-154 may have therapeutic value for the prevention and/or treatment of mammary tumorigensis.
